column1: # S2.2f.1's table, a cell a line: a sentence of one of the six texts and a failure class with a case in it.
# The cells were chosen, and the two model columns judged, before any parser's output was read.
# ref: what the hand's step 1 (einaf/contract/<text>/step1.ein) writes, the reference.
# M1: the model's step 1 in S2.2.2's probe (T2.2.2.8: qwen3.5:4b, thinking off, no grammar, step1.off.<text>).
# M2: the model's step 1 in S2.2.4's steps (runs/steps/<text>/step1.out.ein, under step 1's grammar; bob1 is apples' text;
#     together was not among S2.2.4's texts: n/a).
# Tools: xfm and spring (amrlib's two parse models), ibm (IBM's transition parser), stanza (its UD parse and entities),
#     spacy (en_core_web_trf: UPOS, its own dependency scheme, entities), coref (Stanza's coreference across the text),
#     wsd (WordNet senses chosen by a trained T5, with the sense's hypernyms).
# A declaration's labels carry the kind of its argument places, as a membership does.
# A verdict: R right, W wrong, N not carried (the analysis says nothing of it, or a kind that is no kind, `Thing`),
#     n/a no run. A model's verdict `W|R` is wrong as the class defines it and right on the reading alone (the fault
#     is Ein's writing, e.g. a number written as a name). A tool's `-`: its layer does not speak to the class
#     (coref and wsd outside theirs), counted as N.
